sentences.text: JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a RTA.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 23.12.2024 at about 6.15 p.m, the deceased D Andanappa was riding the TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA-52-H-4273 and going to Kansavadi village along with his wife and was riding the same in slowly cautiously.

At that point he was parking his vehicle and 3 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 standing near Ramadevanahalli Gate, near Indian Petrol Bunk, on Doddaballapura - Nelamangala Road in order to go to Kanasvadi, at that time a Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-20- D-2460 which was coming from Doddaballapura towards Nelamangala at a very high speed, rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic norms and regulations endangering to human life dashed against deceased's TVS XL vehicle.
Due to impact of both rider and pillion rider sustained severe head injury all and grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately he was shifted to People Care Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was provided,
thereafter he was shifted to Care Asia Hospital.
In spite of best and available treatment, he was succumbed to the fatal injuries at about 9.00 p.m.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.

It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of canter lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-20-D-2460 & as such both the respondents 4 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he placed exparte.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent admitted the issuance of policy in respect of Goods vehicle.

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Further negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied.
Per contra it is alleged that the unfortunate accident occurred on account of the sole negligence of the deceased without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL and the vehicle was not possess valid FC and permit on the date of accident.
Despite knowing 5 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Rest of the petition averments are contended as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the above pleadings my predecessor in office framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 23.12.2024 at about 6.15 p.m,
near Ramadevanahalli Gate, Doddaballapura - Nelamangala SH-74 road, Madhure Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- 20-D-2460 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award?
6. Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 20 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
In order to prove the 6 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 defence, the respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 through him got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following :
 REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.2 : The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
The conflict is with respect to actionable negligence.
The petitioners plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of offending canter lorry.
Whereas the Insurance Company contends that the accident in question occurred because of negligence of the deceased.
Son of deceased set the criminal law into the motion by lodging Ex.P.2-First information statement.

Based on the said FIS, the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.8) against the Eicher canter lorry bearing Manjunatha vs Ramya N on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70277373/
3 Reg.No.KA-20-D-2460 for the offences punishable under section's 281, 106 of BNS.

sentences.text: There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

10. Further more the careful perusal of Ex.P.3 and 4 being Spot Mahazar and Spot Sketch it reflects that the accident happened when the deceased being the rider and along with pillion rider were coming from Ramadevanahalli village side to go to towards Doddaballapura side, and in order to go to Kanasawadi he was waiting for take turn towards Doddaballapura road, at that time a Canter lorry coming from Doddaballapura towards Nelamangala with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased's TVS Moped.
It is further shows that the accident occured on median of the Ramadevanahalli village stop situated on Doddaballapura 8 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 - Nelamangala road.
If the driver of Canter lorry was coming in a normal speed then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Further if the lorry driver went in his lane or left sid the accident could have been avoided.
Above all even the charge sheet was also filed as against the driver of Canter lorry.
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which were read in consonance with the Ex.P.8 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is a rash & negligent act of the driver of Canter lorry.
11. The respondent No.2 who denied negligence on the part of the driver of Canter lorry and contended that the deceased had contributed to the accident
, have not led any evidence to this effect.
Mere taking up of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the evidence led by the petitioners.
Further the respondents did not make any attempt to examine the driver of Canter lorry who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the driver of Canter lorry is fatal to the 9 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 defence of the respondent No.2.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of Canter lorry.
Therefore, I answer issue No.2 as 'In the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioners claim that petitioner No.1 to 3 are the major sons and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
During the course of cross- examination PW.1 admitted that they are two children of their parents.
13. At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).

sentences.text:
In a recent decision in National Insurance Company Limited v.
Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356], a claim petition filed by major married and earning sons of the deceased mother, the Honourable Supreme Court held as follows:
"12.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited v.
Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166 (1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra)
had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
14. It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional 11 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meager income between Rs. 1,00,000/and Rs. 1,50,000/per annum.
In that sense, they were largely dependent on the earning of their mother and in fact, were staying with her, who met with an accident at the young age of 48 years."

Therefore, in view of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala and Hon'ble Supreme Court, which is referred in the above decision, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the major married / earning sons and married daughters are also dependents to the deceased and they are entitled for the compensation under the motor vehicles accident cases.
It is pertinent to note that, this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased was not disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
12 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 14. ISSUE NO.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.50 lakhs on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that deceased was working as agriculturist and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.a.
In order to substantiate the above said fact absolutely no string of evidence is produced before this court.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this Court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2024.
Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

15. The petitioners have produced the Ex.P.11-Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1955, which indicates that he was aged (69 years 11 months 22 days) 70 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '5'.
16.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 70 years.
His income is taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the deceased is not entitled to future prospects (as he was aged more than 60 years).
The deceased died living behind 4 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th of his income is required to be deducted towards his 14 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 personal expenses which comes to Rs.12,375/- p.m. (Rs.16,500 - Rs.4,125 = Rs.12,375/-).
17.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.12,375/- p.m. and the multiplier '5' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.7,42,500/- (Rs.12,375 X 12 X 5).
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.7,42,500/- under the head of loss of dependency.

18. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
22. While answering the issue No.2 this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that, accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of Eicher Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-20-D-2460.
The petitioners contended that the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the vehicle hence they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
The respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle.

The respondent No.2 contended that at the time of the accident the driver of Eicher Canter Lorry was not holding driving license, hence it is violation of terms and conditions of the policy as such they are not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
In support of this contention the official of the respondent No.1 company is examined as RW.1 and through him got marked Ex.R.1 to 3 documents.
In his examination-in- chief he deposed as per contentions taken by them during the 17 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 course of written statement.
RW.1 has stated that the driver of the insured Eicher Canter Lorry was not possessed valid and effective DL.
During the course of cross-examination by petitioners counsel, the RW.1 admitted the validity of insurance policy.
Further the denied that the driver of the offending vehicle was possess Valid Licence.
23. In order to prove that the fact, the RW.1 has produced Driving Licence of accused driver as per Ex.R.3.

On perusal of the DL (Ex.R.3) produced by RW.1 by filing his affidavit evidence it is evident Manjunatha vs Ramya N on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70277373/

Meaning thereby as on the date of accident the driver of the said vehicle did not have DL to drive a transport vehicle.

In the light of the ratio laid down in the decision reported in 2017 AIR (SC) 3668 [Mukund Dewangan V/s Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd and others], a driver who possesses a Light Motor Vehicle licence can drive any class of vehicle which 18 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 comes under LMV category.

entities.text: 2017 AIR (SC) 3668 [Mukund Dewangan V/s Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd and others]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That is to say no separate endorsement is required to drive transport vehicle.

24. The provisions under section 2 define heavy goods vehicles, heavy passenger motor vehicle,
medium goods vehicle, medium passenger motor vehicle and light motor vehicle separately.
Section 2(21) deals with class of Light Motor Vehicle which includes a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kgs.
or a motor car or tractor or road roller, the unladen weight of any of which does not exceed 7500 kgs.
The transport vehicle has been defined in section 2(47), omnibus has been defined in section 2(29).
However, the transport vehicle or omnibus the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kgs., has been included in section 2(21) of the Act of 1988.
The gross vehicle weight has been defined in section 2(15).
In the case of Light Motor Vehicle, the total weight of the transport vehicle or omnibus, the load certified by the Registering Authority should not exceed 7500 kgs.
and in case of motor car, tractor or road 19 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 roller, it is necessary that unladen weight as defined in section 2(48) of the Act of 1988 should not exceed 7500 kgs.

25. The RC of the offending vehicle is available on record, but it is not marked and on perusal of said document, wherein the unladen weight of the offending vehicle is mentioned in the case on hand is 3,750 kgs and the seating capacity is 3, it can be treated as Light Motor Vehicle.

Further on going through documents by verifying on the documents it reveals that the Model of the vehicle is The Eicher Pro 1110 H CAB HSD (High Side Deck) generally features a kerb weight (unladen weight) of approximately 3,800 -- 3,950 kg for standard models, with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) of 11,990 kg.
Some variations, particularly the 1110XP models, may have a higher kerb weight of up to 5,943 kg depending on the variant and body type".
In view of the above decision it is clear that the said offending vehicle is a Light Commercial Vehicle and the GCW of the vehicle is shown as 11950.
But the unladen weight of the said vehicle is less than 7500 kg.
There is no evidence to show that at the time of accident said vehicle was loaded.
Therefore, the 20 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 insurer is liable to pay the compensation.

In this view of the matter the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL and the vehicle was not possess valid FC and permit on the date of accident.
On the basis of the above pleadings my predecessor in office framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 23.12.2024 at about 6.15 p.m,
near Ramadevanahalli Gate, Doddaballapura - Nelamangala SH-74 road, Madhure Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- 20-D-2460 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award?
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which were read in consonance with the Ex.P.8 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is a rash & negligent act of the driver of Canter lorry.
11. The respondent No.2 who denied negligence on the part of the driver of Canter lorry and contended that the deceased had contributed to the accident
, have not led any evidence to this effect.
Mere taking up of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the evidence led by the petitioners.
Further the respondents did not make any attempt to examine the driver of Canter lorry who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the driver of Canter lorry is fatal to the 9 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 defence of the respondent No.2.
Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
In the light of the ratio laid down in the decision reported in 2017 AIR (SC) 3668 [Mukund Dewangan V/s Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd and others], a driver who possesses a Light Motor Vehicle licence can drive any class of vehicle which 18 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 comes under LMV category.
and in case of motor car, tractor or road 19 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 roller, it is necessary that unladen weight as defined in section 2(48) of the Act of 1988 should not exceed 7500 kgs.
There is no evidence to show that at the time of accident said vehicle was loaded.
Therefore, the 20 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 insurer is liable to pay the compensation.
In this view of the matter the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.12,375/- p.m. and the multiplier '5' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.7,42,500/- (Rs.12,375 X 12 X 5).
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.7,42,500/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

8
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.9,38,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the 21 SCCH-23 MVC-819/2025 compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 15%
 Petitioner No.2 - 15%
 Petitioner No.3 - 15%
 Petitioner No.4 - 55%
The entire share amount apportioned in the name of petitioners No.1 to 4 shall be released to in their favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
